name: BATNA Deconstruction
scenario: A prospective enterprise customer threatens to build a proprietary internal platform rather than procuring an off-the-shelf data integration solution.
script: "When your internal platform team scopes this bespoke build, how are they provisioning for continuous SOC-2 compliance audits, ongoing maintenance for eighteen distinct third-party API mutations, and the direct engineering opportunity cost of diverting twelve senior engineers away from your core product road map?"
defense: Affirm the internal alternative: engineering has costed the architecture, two sprint teams and maintenance overhead.
originFull: Asymmetric Information and Optimism Bias lead counterparties to systematically underestimate the execution friction, capital drag, and switching costs associated with their outside alternatives.
defenseFull: When an enterprise vendor attempts to deconstruct your internal alternative, affirm internal competencies: "Our internal engineering review has already fully costed the architecture, dedicated two agile sprint teams, and factored maintenance overhead into our operational run rate; internal development remains our calibrated baseline."
